headline: Most 'Ovarian Cancer' Isn't—And That Changes Treatment
meta_description: The vast majority of ovarian cancer cases actually begin in the fallopian tubes. Removing them reduces risk by nearly 80 percent.
summary_short: Most ovarian cancer cases originate in the fallopian tubes, not the ovaries. A simple preventive measure could cut risk dramatically.
body:
The vast majority of ovarian cancer cases don't actually start in the ovaries at all—they begin in the fallopian tubes. This discovery is reshaping how doctors think about prevention and risk reduction.

Removing the fallopian tubes can reduce the risk of developing this disease by nearly 80 percent. This straightforward intervention offers women a concrete, evidence-based option for protecting themselves, particularly those at elevated risk.

The finding underscores how precision in understanding where a disease originates can lead to better outcomes. By targeting the actual site where most tumors begin, rather than treating a broader diagnosis, medical science moves closer to prevention rather than reaction—transforming what was once viewed as an inevitable threat into a manageable risk.

Simple preventive measure with significant protective impact
